title: Escapewheel schema registry
description: Shape of logical_schemas.json. Validates the registry document; column semantics are values within it, not JSON Schema types.

$schema.description: The meta-schema this document conforms to. Identity, not a fetch instruction -- a validator MUST NOT dereference it.

extension_id.description: Present on an extension registry; namespaces its tables.

extends.description: The logical standard version this extension was written against.

primary_key.description: Column names, or null for a table admitting duplicate rows.

type.description: The Arrow-compatible type vocabulary. Nested types are forbidden.

presence.description: required: present, non-null. nullable: present, may be null. optional: may be absent.

role.description: What kind of thing the column holds, which decides what a consumer may do with it -- notably whether a 1-based client converts it at the boundary. Closed: a consumer derives behaviour from it, so an unrecognised value would be unsafe. A discriminator holds a dotted resource ID naming a table, which a consumer resolves to decide what the row means.

resolves.description: Required on a discriminator, and only there. `required`: a value naming no declared resource leaves the row uninterpretable. `optional`: it is a fact -- the thing is not a packet resource.

discriminates.description: On a paired-value discriminator, the column holding an identifier in the named table's key space. Absent where the discriminated row shares the named table's key.

enum.description: Closed value set. A validator MUST reject values outside it.

vocabulary.description: Which vocabulary the values are drawn from. closed: the column also declares `enum` and a validator MUST reject anything outside it. open: the values name kinds of thing, comparable between packets, and a validator MUST NOT reject an unrecognised one. free: not a vocabulary at all -- a name, a description, a URI, a digest. Required on every string column but a discriminator, whose value space is the declared resource identifiers.

reserved_values.description: Values with fixed meanings within an open vocabulary. Not a closed set.

determined_by.description: Columns whose values determine this one, so that rows agreeing on them agree here. An empty list declares a constant. Used to decide whether a table's sort order puts duplicate primary keys next to each other: a sort column that is determined by key columns cannot separate two rows that share a key.

identity.description: Whether an identifier's value is the source's own (`carried`) or a number this format chose (`assigned`). Not derivable -- a source may supply an integer that the writer replaces -- and it decides whether the table owes a `*_name`. Required where role is identifier, meaningless otherwise.

unit.description: The unit this column's values are in, where it does not vary. Open.

unit_from.description: The column carrying this column's unit, where it varies per row. Either a column of this table, or `resource.column` resolved through a reference this table declares -- one hop.

clock_from.description: The column holding the `clock_id` these ticks are on. Absent, the clock is the table's own `clock_id` where it has one. Coordinates only.

discriminates_via.description: Where a discriminator sits a reference away from the rows it specialises, the referencing column as `resource.column`.

positions_in.description: On a by-position discriminator, the column of this table whose value is the position column in the named resource. Absent on the other two shapes, and never beside `discriminates`.

authority.description: The nomenclatures this column's values are spelled by, each declaring the name a person reads and the URI a document resolves. The URI is identity, not a fetch instruction: a validator MUST NOT dereference one and MUST NOT reject a value for being absent from it. An array because a column's values may be drawn from more than one registry.

sql.description: Returns offending rows; empty is a pass.

advisory.description: Off by default; runs only when the caller asks. Never `error`, so enabling advisories cannot change whether a packet passed.
